text:
jules: FYI onboarding update for Atelier's LoRA merge (atelier-7b-lora). ran the quickpack/compat smoke and seeing a formatting regression on monetary values after int4 quant + merge. attaching notes below.

tasha: ugh, can you paste the failing examples?

jules: sure — short repro from the eval pack: model asked to normalize amounts, before merge/int4 it returned `"$1,200.00"`, after merge+int4 it returns `"1200"` or `"1.2k"` inconsistently. this breaks the downstream parser.

samir: is that a tokenizer shift or decoding artifact? sounds like tokenization/byte pair boundary changed. did you run the token alignment check from the onboarding checklist?

jules: ran tokenmap-check.sh and diffed token ids for the prompt prefix. small deltas at positions 14-16 for commas/periods. output: ```diff --token-ids prompt-prefix.tokens before: [34,56,78,12,9] after: [34,56,99,12,9]```

jenna: interesting. could be the LoRA merge touching the embedding/ln weights causing subtle rounding differences that the int4 comp amplifies. any quantization config differences vs baseline?

jules: same quant config used for previous merges: qconfig="nf4-v2, clip=0.995, group=128". used our standard merge flow: `merge_lora --base atelier-7b --lora client/atelier-lora.safetensors --out merged.safetensors`.

samir: can you try the merge but export with int8 (w/ per-channel scale) to see if it reproduces? that'd help isolate int4 quant coupling.

jules: yeah doing that now. kicking off quick repro job: 
```
# run quick eval pack
python -m ri_eval.run --model merged.safetensors --quant int4 --eval-pack ateliersmoke.json --limit 200
```

ci-bot: test job started: eval-1778889000-atelier-smoke (ETA ~ 4m) :gear:

jenna: also check the KV-cache alignment test (long-prefix) — if merges touched rotary/pos-emb offsets, int4 might shift generated token boundaries for numerics.

tasha: if int8 doesn't reproduce, we can safely attribute to int4 sensitivity and recommend a fallthrough plan: either ship int8 for this customer or tweak per-channel clip/gamma.

jules: quick results: int4 run reproduced issue (precision drop), int8 run did not — int8 outputs preserved `$1,200.00` consistently. summary numbers: 
- accuracy (amount format exact-match): baseline (pre-merge int4): 0.98
- merged int4: 0.72
- merged int8: 0.96

samir: that strongly suggests quantization-induced amplification of merge deltas. next steps: try increasing group size for int4 to 1024 and re-run. also test fallback policy for customer route (prefer int8 or dedicated pool).

jules: trying group=1024 + clip 0.999: queued. also added a small eval to check hallucination on numeric tokens and currency symbols.

jenna: any chance this is from LoRA merge order? we previously saw order-dependent overlays when LoRA modifies LayerNorm scales. can you re-run merge with `--preserve-ln` option?

jules: good call. re-merging with `merge_lora --preserve-ln ...` now.

ci-bot: eval job finished: eval-1778889000-atelier-smoke (int4 group=128) — regression confirmed. logs: `amt_ematch: 0.72 -> FAIL`

jules: merged+preserve-ln + int4 (group=128) result: amt_ematch 0.85 — partial improvement. group=1024 run still ongoing.

tasha: that's promising. document suggestion for customer: default to merged-int8 on Dedicated until we have safe int4 profile. also add a canary rule that routes 10% traffic to int4 only after passing the token-formatting regression suite.

samir: please file a short KB note with the evalpack id and seed so we can reproduce later. include the exact commands used and the eval snippet that fails.

jules: will do — evalpack id `atelier-smoke-1778889000`, seed 42. reproducer command: 
```
python -m ri_eval.run --model merged_preserveln.safetensors --quant int4 --group 128 --clip 0.995 --eval-pack ateliersmoke.json --seed 42
```

jenna: would also be good to add a lightweight unit test to the eval harness that asserts currency formatting for top-k candidates — prevents regressions from slipping.

jules: added a TODO in the deck. next actions: 1) finish group=1024 run, 2) if that passes (>=0.95), propose int4 profile update, else default customer to int8 + schedule deeper root cause (merge ordering + ln behavior). I'll ping infra for a canary rollout if we decide to push.

tasha: thanks. @samir want to sign off on the fallback policy?

samir: +1 on fallback to int8 and canary gating. also loop-in the model-onboard PM for release notes.

jenna: thanks everyone. small note — remind customer they'll see slightly higher latency on int8 but no correctness hit.

jules: noted. I'll post the final summary and attach the eval json once group=1024 finishes. :white_check_mark:
